movement_source: row 'Common Equity Tier 1 (APRA) (%)', column 31 Dec 24 -> column 31 Dec 25
headline: CBA's APRA Level 2 (Group) CET1 ratio rose 10 bpts over the year, from 12.2% at 31 Dec 24 to 12.3% at 31 Dec 25, and was unchanged on 30 Jun 25 (ev-24, ev-9, ev-14, ev-12). CET1 Capital grew to $61,922m from $58,871m while total RWA rose 5% to $505,310m from $482,369m (ev-36, ev-25, ev-22). CBA publishes NO 12-month CET1 walk: both the results book and the slides show only the half-on-half Jun 25 → Dec 25 bridge (Cash NPAT +107, 2H25 dividend -87, RWA -33, Other +9 bpts), so its bars cannot be this comparison's contributions (ev-1..ev-5). Two events with their own printed bpts sit inside the 12-month window: adoption of the revised APS 117 IRRBB framework on 1 Oct 2025 (~$10bn RWA reduction, +24 bpts) and the on-market DRP purchase for the 2025 final dividend ($643m, -13 bpts) (ev-10, ev-11). Context: Level 1 CET1 12.1%→12.2%; internationally comparable CET1 18.8%→18.3% — different measures (ev-16, ev-17).

drivers.columns: footnoted bpts impact, event dated 1 Oct 2025
drivers.narrative: The bank footnotes "the reduction to IRRBB RWA of ~$10 billion (CET1 impact of +24 bpts) on adoption of the revised APS 117 framework effective 1 October 2025" (ev-10). IRRBB RWA fell to $35,179m from $41,679m at Dec 24 (ev-20); the half-on-half fall of $4.7bn/12% was "partly offset by the impact of higher long-term interest rates in Australia reducing embedded gains" (ev-31).

drivers.columns: footnoted bpts impact, 2025 final dividend in 1H26
drivers.narrative: "The 2025 final dividend included the on-market purchase of $643 million of shares (CET1 impact of -13 bpts) in respect of the Dividend Reinvestment Plan" (ev-11); DRP participation was 14.8% (ev-34). This is the DRP-neutralisation cost only, not the whole dividend: the full 2H25 dividend bar is -87 bpts in the Jun 25→Dec 25 walk (ev-1), and DPS was 235c in 1H26 versus 225c in 1H25 (ev-27).

The bank names "Capital generated from earnings" as a key driver but quantifies it only half-on-half: Cash NPAT +107 bpts for Jun 25→Dec 25 (ev-1, ev-12 page). Cash NPAT from continuing operations was $5,445m in 1H26, up 6% on $5,132m in 1H25 (ev-28); the walk bar "Excludes net equity accounted profits/losses and impairments from associates as they are capital neutral" (ev-7). No 12-month bpts figure is published.

Total RWA rose 5% to $505,310m from $482,369m at Dec 24 (ev-25, ev-22), a headwind the bank quantifies only half-on-half (RWA -33 bpts, Jun 25→Dec 25: Credit -34, IRRBB +11, Operational -9, Market -1; ev-1..ev-5). Over 12 months Credit RWA rose 6% to $409,119m (ev-26), Operational risk RWA to $51,041m from $47,624m (ev-21) and Traded market risk to $9,971m from $7,949m (ev-19).

Credit risk RWA rose 6% to $409,119m from $385,117m at Dec 24 (ev-26, ev-18). The bank's stated drivers are half-on-half only: "increased $10.2 billion or 2.6% on the prior half" from volume growth of $17.3bn "across commercial portfolios, domestic residential mortgages, and New Zealand portfolios" and data & methodology +$4.9bn "due to an increase in the residential mortgage overlay", offset by credit quality -$6.5bn "primarily from lower risk weights for residential mortgages" (ev-30, ev-33). Dec 25 includes an $8.0bn residential mortgage PD model overlay (ev-23).

Operational risk RWA rose to $51,041m at Dec 25 from $47,624m at Dec 24 (ev-21), all of it in 1H26: "the increase in Operational Risk RWA by $3.4 billion or 7.2% on the prior half to $51.0 billion was primarily driven by higher average net interest income over the years ended 30 June 2025, 2024 and 2023 due to higher interest rates and lending growth" (ev-32). Half-on-half CET1 cost -9 bpts (ev-5).

Traded market risk RWA rose to $9,971m from $7,949m at Dec 24 (ev-19). The bank quantifies the CET1 effect only half-on-half at -1 bpt (ev-4) and gives no reason beyond noting increases in Traded Market Risk RWA alongside Credit and Operational risk (ev-29). No 12-month bpts figure and no stated cause are disclosed.

The bank lists "Other regulatory adjustments and movement in reserves" as a key driver, quantified only half-on-half at +9 bpts and defined as including "intangibles, FX impact on Credit RWA, equity accounted profits/losses and impairments from associates, movements in reserves and other regulatory adjustments" (ev-1, ev-8). Over 12 months total CET1 regulatory adjustments improved to -$15,439m from -$16,522m, with the equity investments deduction falling to $3,289m from $4,225m and the cash flow hedge reserve at $1,113m versus $590m (ev-37, ev-39, ev-38).

Capital returns contributed nothing across the window: "No share buy-back activity was undertaken during 1H26 and 2H25" (ev-35), and only $300m of the $1bn on-market buy-back announced 9 August 2023 had been completed by 31 Dec 25 (ev-13). No buy-back bar appears in the capital walk (ev-1).

notable_items: Revised APS 117 IRRBB framework adopted 1 October 2025: ~$10bn IRRBB RWA reduction, +24 bpts CET1 (ev-10)
2025 final dividend DRP satisfied by $643m on-market purchase: -13 bpts (ev-11)
$8.0bn RWA overlay on the Australian Residential Mortgage PD model at 31 Dec 25 (ev-23)

disagreements.topic: CET1 measure variant: internationally comparable ratio moves the opposite way
disagreements.explanation: The internationally comparable CET1 ratio applies Basel-framework adjustments to APRA's more conservative framework and is a different measure; the task's headline measure is the APRA Level 2 (Group) ratio from the results book KPI table (ev-24, ev-17).
Level 1 is the parent-bank consolidation, a different measure quoted as context only (ev-16).

limitations: CBA publishes no CET1 walk for the task comparison (Dec 24 -> Dec 25). Both the results book (p.28) and the slides (pp.33, 103) show only the Jun 25 -> Dec 25 half-on-half bridge, which read_chart classified as context. Its bars (Cash NPAT +107, 2H25 dividend -87, RWA -33, Other +9) are therefore described inside narratives, never used as contributions.

Consequently only the two footnoted, period-matching events are quantified (+24 bpts APS 117; -13 bpts DRP on-market purchase). These do not, and are not intended to, sum to the +10 bpts movement; the residual of roughly -1 bpt is nominal and the true unexplained portion is essentially the whole movement.

The -13 bpts dividend figure covers only the DRP neutralisation of the 2025 final dividend, not the gross dividend paid; the 1H25 interim dividend paid during 2H25 (also DRP-neutralised, 18.1% participation) sits inside the 12-month window but its bpts impact is not separately disclosed.

The read_chart sum check on the half-on-half walk FAILED (1230 + (-4) = 1226 vs printed end 1230), consistent with the bank's own note that "numbers presented in this section may not sum precisely to the totals provided" due to rounding.

The bank states IRRBB's APS 117 benefit was "partly offset by the impact of higher long-term interest rates in Australia reducing embedded gains", so the +24 bpts gross benefit exceeds the net IRRBB contribution (+11 bpts half-on-half).

The Cash NPAT walk bar excludes equity accounted profits/losses and impairments from associates (capital neutral) and the Credit RWA bar excludes FX, which is carried in 'Other' - so those bars are not comparable to the reported P&L or RWA totals.
No divestment or acquisition CET1 bpts impact is disclosed for the window; no such bar appears in the published walk.
RWA figures in the corpus quotes are printed in $M/$bn; the $m unit tag on those evidence numbers reflects the tool's unit vocabulary, not a restatement.
Capped at 80: dividend_net_drp -13 bps. Each of these claims cites a walk whose own bars do not sum to that chart's endpoints, so the read it rests on disagrees with itself.
